diagnostic_evidence.quote: To simplify the presentation, we assume throughout that \(\Omega\) is sufficiently large so that \(\operatorname{supp}u(\cdot,t)\subset\Omega\) for all \(t\in[0,T]\). This allows us to ignore boundary effects.

issues.failure_explanation: Summing the cellwise identity over all cells produces, besides the t=0, t=T and Γ_j faces, the lateral boundary integral ∫_{∂Ω×(0,T)} (F(u_{θ*})-F(ũ_h))sgn(u_{θ*}-ũ_h)·n ds. Only the exact solution u (hence ũ_h) is assumed to vanish near ∂Ω; the network u_{θ*} is unconstrained there, since the loss penalizes only initial data, the interior residual and the entropy surrogate. This term is O(1) with uncontrolled sign (e.g. for Burgers with u_{θ*}≈-1 at the right boundary it equals -(1/2)T), so the inequality ‖u_{θ*}(T)-ũ_h(T)‖ ≤ ‖u_{θ*}(0)-ũ_h(0)‖+C(h+M^{-1}+Mh) does not follow. Indeed, the competitor construction of Lemma lem:Lu_shock applies verbatim to the entropy solution of the same initial-value problem with inflow boundary data on ∂Ω (which differs from u by O(1) in L^1 at time T), giving it loss ≲ h as well; hence L(θ*) ≲ h alone cannot imply closeness to u. The same omission occurs in every stability proof (eq:part1_Lu_rarefaction, eq:md_error_identity, eq:shock_birth_error_identity).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a lateral boundary penalty (e.g. ∫_{∂Ω×(0,T)}|v| ds) to the loss or restrict the network class to functions vanishing on ∂Ω×(0,T), require dist(supp u(·,t),∂Ω) ≳ h so the CPwL competitors vanish there, and include the lateral term in each ibp identity, bounding it by the penalty (≲ h).

issues.title: Lateral space-time boundary terms dropped in the stability identity; loss does not control u_theta on ∂Ω×(0,T)
issues.why_classification: The method's loss functional and every stability proof must be modified, but the fix is a standard additional penalty, the same proof architecture works and all rates survive.

issues.failure_explanation: V_h^c is defined with an arbitrary fixed constant c>0, and the theorems impose no relation between c and u. The test function ũ_h (an interpolant of u and of its smooth extensions, plus a tip/event patch with h|∇ũ_h| ≤ C) lies in V_h^c only if c ≥ ‖u‖_{L^∞}+O(1). For small c the choice k_h=ũ_h in (eq:min_loss) is not admissible and the stability argument collapses; the appendix itself acknowledges the need to enlarge c. The same gap affects the ũ_h constructions in the rarefaction, compound, birth, 1D-main and multi-D theorems.

issues.overall_effect: The error estimates hold only for c sufficiently large depending on u; as stated (arbitrary fixed c) they are unproven.
issues.title: Membership ũ_h ∈ V_h^c requires the bound c to be large relative to the exact solution; hypothesis missing from theorems

rarefaction pieces contribute $O(h|\ln h|)$, and compound wave pieces contribute

issues.failure_explanation: No proof is given. Following the announced strategy, the competitor loss is O(h|ln h|) (rarefaction part), so ∫|∇·F(u_{θ*})| ≲ |ln h| and the strip-selection remainder is |ln h|/M; the shifted-trace term on the fan side involves |∇u| ~ 1/t and yields Mh|ln h| (exactly as in eq:shock_birth_shifted_trace_est). Balancing gives h^{1/2}|ln h|, which is what the appendix proof of thm:main_1d actually asserts for compound-wave pieces. The stated (h|ln h|)^{1/2} is better by a factor |ln h|^{1/2} and is not supported by anything in the source; the two statements are mutually inconsistent.

failure_location.quote: The proof follows the same strategy as a single shock (Theorem~\ref{thm:shock}) and a single rarefaction (Theorem~\ref{thm:rarefaction}), so we omit the details.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either weaken (eq:compound_wave_result) to C h^{1/2}|ln h| (consistent with thm:main_1d), or supply an explicit construction (e.g. an extension of the fan branch with vanishing shift error along the shock) proving the sharper rate.

issues.failure_explanation: Between Γ_j(t_h) and the true shock Γ(t_h) (a segment of length up to jL ≲ Mh ≈ h^{1/2}), cells below t=t_h interpolate u (the left branch) while cells above interpolate u_ext^+; these differ by O(1) (the shock strength plus extension error), so ũ_h jumps across that horizontal face. This face term is missing from (eq:shock_birth_error_identity) and the claimed continuity statement is false. Its contribution is bounded by C·Mh = O(h^{1/2}), which is within the final budget, but it must be added to the identity.

issues.overall_effect: The error identity (eq:shock_birth_error_identity) is incomplete; after adding the O(Mh) face term the stated rate h^{1/2}|ln h| is unaffected.
issues.title: Shock-birth test function ũ_h has an unaccounted jump across the face t=t_h between Γ_j and Γ

issues.failure_explanation: The proof chooses open sets U_q with closure inside each non-smooth piece P_q, sets Ω_reg = Ω_T∖∪U_q, and takes the nodal interpolant of u on Ω_reg, asserting u ∈ W^{2,∞}∩C^2 there and that the local constructions can be matched on ∂U_q. But by Assumption assump:piecewise_smooth shocks traverse piece boundaries (a shock born in a birth piece continues into the adjacent regular shock piece; interaction pieces receive incoming shocks from regular shock pieces). Hence the portion of each such shock near ∂P_q is not covered by any U_q, u is discontinuous on Ω_reg, and its P^1 interpolant neither has small residual nor matches the strip-based competitors on ∂U_q. Step 2 (global DPwP ũ_h) has the analogous gap: shifted mesh-aligned interfaces from different pieces must be made globally consistent along a single shock, which is not addressed.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reorganize the patching along whole wave curves rather than per piece: build the ε-strip and the strip-selection/shifted interface globally along each entire shock curve (with the local event treatments at its endpoints), and verify conformity and the uniform W_h^{1,∞} bounds of the resulting global ũ_h.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem thm:main_1d does not establish the global competitor and test-function constructions for any configuration in which a shock passes between pieces, i.e. essentially every multi-piece solution; the global O(h^{1/2}|ln h|) estimate is unproven as written.
